answer: A time capsule is sealed beneath the observatory pier, and its contents are listed in the foundation charter kept by the trustees. A prism capsule buried in a garden fails the charter: at the horizon of the stone the contents must match the list the trustees hold, and a garden capsule holds whatever the forger fancied. Forging the charter means bribing a trustee, faking 30 years of minutes and paying 24,800, and the haven seal on the charter is broken only at the centenary, so a capsule whose contents were never listed is dug up and emptied.
